lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: key features of graphs and tables
lessonRef.title: Targeted correction: key features of graphs and tables

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Each example contains the correction, not just the answer.

items.prompt: C(h) = 100 − 20h, machine runs at most 10 hours. Domain?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Before solving, say which error the problem is testing for.

items.prompt: In a modelling context, the graph of a projectile’s height against time crosses the horizontal axis. Which feature is this, and what does it mean?
choices: the maximum, giving the greatest height
the y-intercept, giving the launch height
a zero, giving the time the projectile returns to ground level
the average rate of change over the flight

items.prompt: Does the set {(1, 4), (2, 4), (3, 4), (5, 4)} define y as a function of x? Justify the decision.
choices: No; the input 4 gives both y = 2 and y = −2.
No; the input 1 is paired with both 3 and 8.
Yes; repeated outputs are allowed, only repeated inputs with different outputs are not.
Yes; each input appears once, so each has exactly one output.

items.prompt: A machine starts with 150 components and consumes 5 per hour. It can run for at most 8 hours. What is the domain of C(h) = 150 − 5h in this context?
choices: all real numbers

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A sequence is defined by a(1) = 4 and a(n) = a(n − 1) − 5 for n > 1. Find a(8).
In a modelling context, the graph of a cooling object’s temperature flattens out towards a horizontal line. Which feature is this, and what does it mean?
choices: a maximum, giving the hottest temperature
an end behaviour approaching the surrounding temperature
an interval of increase
a zero, giving the time the object freezes

items.prompt: Does the set {(1, 3), (2, 5), (1, 8), (4, 9)} define y as a function of x? Justify the decision.
choices: No; the input 1 is paired with both 3 and 8.
Yes; each input appears once, so each has exactly one output.
No; the input 4 gives both y = 2 and y = −2.
Yes; repeated outputs are allowed, only repeated inputs with different outputs are not.
